narrative:
The model estimates a 58% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background.

Your extensive overall experience of more than 11 years was the strongest factor pushing the model toward predicting you would leave. While only 14.7% of employees predicted to stay have this level of total experience, the model sees long-tenured professionals as more likely to explore new opportunities elsewhere.

Your relatively short time in your current role (1-5 years) was the second most influential factor and also increased the likelihood of leaving. This is notably lower than the tenure of many employees the model expects to stay.

The third important factor worked in the opposite direction: you have not received other job offers while at this company. This lack of external opportunities slightly reduced the predicted chance of leaving. However, it was not enough to outweigh the first two factors.

The organization should consider discussing your long-term career goals with you and exploring whether additional responsibilities or growth opportunities could increase your sense of attachment to the company. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying more appealing in the long run. (218 words)
